Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa (Zimmermann Salesforce PWA Kit, TypeScript overrides on top of `@salesforce/retail-react-app`). Read-only investigation only — no edits.

I'm planning to build a demo page on the homepage that renders a shared `ZimmProductCard` component (organism, at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx`) in all its variant/state combinations, using real, live SFCC product data (not fixtures — this project's own AGENTS.md forbids mocking in production paths). Need to understand the current state of the homepage override and this codebase's established container/page pattern before designing anything.

Investigate and report back:

1. **Does `overrides/app/pages/home/` (or similar) exist today?** If so, read it in full and report exactly what it currently renders — the user described it as "the current blank homepage." Also check `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/home/` (the base SFCC home page this would override) to understand what it normally does, and what — if anything — this project's own override currently changes about it.

2. **Is `overrides/app/routes.tsx` involved at all for the homepage route**, or does the homepage route resolve automatically via the base app's own routing without this repo needing to register anything? Read `overrides/app/routes.tsx` in full and report exactly what it currently contains (route list) and whether a `home`/`/`-path route already exists there or is inherited from base untouched.

3. **Find this codebase's own best current example of a PAGE-level container that fetches real commerce-sdk-react data and passes it down as props to presentational components** — per `.claude/rules/components.md`'s rule that data-fetching belongs in `overrides/app/pages/` (or another container), never inside a leaf component under `overrides/app/components/`. The most likely candidate is `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (mentioned in prior work this session as an ~1000+ line file that composes several `ui-kits/` atoms/molecules with real product data) — read it in full, and specifically identify: which `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hook(s) it calls to get real product data (e.g. `useProduct`, `useProducts`, `useCategory`, `useSearchProducts` — whatever it actually uses, don't guess), what the returned data shape looks like, and how it maps that raw SFCC/commerce-sdk response onto the props of the presentational components it renders (is there a dedicated mapper file, e.g. `productInfo.ts`, that does this translation — read that too if it exists).

4. **Check whether any hook already exists in this codebase for fetching a single product's full detail data by ID/slug** (likely `useProduct` from `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`, but confirm by checking how `product-detail`'s page actually calls it) — report the hook's real signature/return shape as used in this codebase (from actual usage, not from guessing at the SDK's docs) so I know what fields would realistically be available to map onto `ZimmProductCardProps` (which needs: `primaryImage`/`hoverImage`/`images` as `{src, alt}` objects, `currentPrice`/`originalPrice` as pre-formatted strings, `colour`/`size` as plain strings, `name`, `href`, `isUnavailable`).

5. **Check whether this codebase already has a currency/price formatting utility** used elsewhere to turn a raw SFCC price number into a display string like "$595.00" (search for how `zimmProductCardContent`'s or `product-detail`'s own consumers currently produce `currentPrice`/`originalPrice` string props — do they format it themselves, or is there a shared `formatPrice`-style utility already in `overrides/app/utils/` or similar).

6. **Read `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` and `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`** to confirm the exact protection tier and named owner for `overrides/app/pages/home/` (or wherever the homepage override would live) and for `overrides/app/routes.tsx` — I need to know whether editing the homepage alone crosses zero protection tiers, or whether it would also require touching the Tier 2 `routes.tsx`.

Report as structured findings with exact file paths, hook names, and prop-mapping shapes — I'm using this directly to design a real implementation plan, so precision on what actually exists (vs. what I'd need to build fresh) matters most.

content.content: 1 # Components, Hooks & Storybook 2 3 Everything about designing, structuring, and presenting a React component or hook in this 4 project. Split out of [conventions.md](./conventions.md) — see that file for cross-cutting 5 rules that apply to every file regardless of type (TypeScript-only, DRY/KISS/SOLID, magic 6 numbers, security). TypeScript idioms live in [typescript.md](./typescript.md); Chakra/CSS 7 conventions live in [css.md](./css.md). 8 9 --- 10 11 ## Components 12 13 - **Named export** matches the folder name (e.g. `productTile/` exports `ProductTile`). 14 No default exports of anonymous functions. 15 - **Props type name** matches the component name: `ProductTileProps` for `ProductTile`, 16 `TopNavProps` for `TopNav`. 17 - **Props type placement:** 18 - _Default:_ declare the `Props` type at the top of the component file. 19 - _Move to `types.ts` in the same folder_ only when (a) the type is consumed by sibling 20 files (story, test, sub-components) **or** (b) it exceeds ~30 lines and mixes with 21 other shared types worth co-locating. 22 - The trigger is _shared consumption_, not line count alone. 23 - **JSDoc** is required on: 24 25 - Any component used by ≥2 callers (shared components — typically Tier 2 in 26 [protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md)). 27 - Any exported hook. 28 - Any utility function with non-obvious behaviour. 29 30 Leaf components used by a single page don't need JSDoc — the prop type is sufficient. 31 32 - **Callback props** follow `onEventName` (e.g. `onAddToCart`, `onClose`). 33 - **Required props are non-optional;** optional props use `?` — no `| undefined` unions 34 for "I forgot to mark it optional." 35 - **Accessibility (JSX) — mechanically enforced by `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`, so get 36 these right at authoring time:** 37 - Every `` needs an `alt` attribute (`alt=""` is fine for purely decorative images). 38 - Every `IconButton` (including wrapped variants like `IconButtonWithRegistration`) needs 39 an `aria-label` — it renders no visible text, so screen readers have nothing else to 40 announce. 41 - Any element with an `onClick` that isn't natively interactive (`div`, `span`, `Box`, 42 `Flex`, `Stack`, `VStack`, `HStack`, `Grid`, `Text`, and similar) needs a `role` 43 attribute at minimum — and for real keyboard operability, also `tabIndex={0}` and an 44 `onKeyDown` handler (or just use a `Button`/native interactive element instead, which 45 is almost always simpler than reimplementing keyboard behaviour). 46 47 --- 48 49 ## Composition — writing a "clean" component 50 51 Rules of thumb for when a component is doing too much and should be split, or when inline 52 state belongs in a custom hook instead. 53 54 - **Complexity / size.** A component function should stay roughly under ~150 lines and 55 avoid deep branching (rule of thumb: ~10-15 cyclomatic complexity — count independent 56 paths through the render logic, not total lines). **This is not currently ESLint-enforced** 57 — `.eslintrc.js` has no `max-lines-per-function` or `complexity` rule configured today, so 58 treat this as a self-check during authoring and something `/code-quality` should flag, not 59 something the build will fail on yet. If this keeps being a problem in practice, adding 60 those two ESLint rules is a cheap follow-up (they're built into ESLint core, no new 61 dependency needed). 62 - **Container/presentational separation.** Anything under `overrides/app/components/` 63 receives data as props — it does not call data-fetching hooks itself (SDK hooks like 64 `useCurrentBasket`/`useCurrentCustomer`/`useProduct`, or any `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` 65 / React Query hook). Data-fetching belongs in `overrides/app/pages/` or another container 66 component, which then passes the result down. This generalizes the existing 67 "no commerce state hooks inside leaf components" rule to _all_ data-fetching, not just 68 commerce SDK hooks — the reasoning is the same either way: a component that owns its own 69 data-fetching can't be reused somewhere the data arrives differently (SSR-prefetched, 70 mocked in Storybook, composed from a parent that already has it). 71 72 **Exception — Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks** (`useIntl`, `useUiCopy`) may 73 be called from any component, including presentational leaves. Both read from a Provider 74 mounted above the route tree, not from a per-page/per-component fetch — so calling one from 75 a leaf doesn't create the SSR/Storybook/parent-composition problem the rule above exists to 76 prevent, and doesn't multiply fetches the way an SDK hook would. `useUiCopy` 77 (`overrides/app/hooks/useUiCopy.ts`, Provider at `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/`) 78 is the reference example — `BottomBar` and `ZimmSubscribeSection` both call it directly 79 for microcopy while still receiving their actual business data as props. This exception is 80 narrow: it covers content that is identical for every consumer regardless of route/context, 81 not anything that varies per page. 82 83 **Their no-Provider behaviour differs, and it matters for tests and stories.** `useUiCopy` 84 degrades to fallback text — `useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY` — so a leaf calling 85 it renders with zero setup. `useIntl` **throws** (`react-intl`'s `invariantIntlContext`: 86 _"Could not find required `intl` object"_), and its `IntlProvider` is mounted by the **base 87 SFCC `_app`**, not by `_app-config` — a strictly narrower subtree. `.storybook/preview.tsx` 88 supplies one for stories precisely because of this; any Vitest test rendering a `useIntl` 89 consumer must wrap it too. An earlier revision of this paragraph claimed both hooks degrade 90 gracefully and that both Providers sit in `_app-config`; neither is true of `useIntl`. 91 - **Extract-to-hook threshold.** Pull inline component logic out into a custom hook 92 (`overrides/app/hooks/use.ts`) when either is true: 93 94 - The component has ≥2 pieces of related `useState` that change together (a strong signal 95 the state belongs in one place, whether that's a custom hook or a single reducer). 96 - Any `useEffect` has a non-trivial dependency array or a cleanup function — non-trivial 97 meaning more than a single obvious dependency, or the effect does anything beyond a 98 one-line side effect. 99 100 This one is judgment-heavy, not a hard mechanical gate — `/code-quality` should flag it as 101 a should-fix, not a must-fix, and a component with ≥4 `useState` calls is a reasonable 102 coarse trigger to at least stop and ask "should this be a hook?" 103 104 --- 105 106 ## Hooks 107 108 - **File extension** is `.ts` (no JSX in a hook file). 109 - **Exported function name** matches the filename: `useWishlist.ts` exports `useWishlist`. 110 - **Parameters and return value are typed** — no implicit `any`, no missing return type. 111 See [typescript.md](./typescript.md) for the general typing rules this extends. 112 - **JSDoc** is required on every exported hook, including a `@returns` description. 113 114 --- 115 116 ## Storybook 117 118 Storybook is the canonical place to view components in isolation. Keep it browsable — 119 a flat 200-story sidebar is unusable. 120 121 ### When a story is required 122 123 - **Required** for any component exported from its folder under `overrides/app/components/` 124 or `overrides/app/pages/` (i.e. anything another file imports). 125 - **Not required** for purely internal sub-components that only render inside one parent 126 (e.g. `productTile/priceRow.tsx` used only by `productTile/index.tsx`). Cover their 127 variants via the parent's stories. 128 - Pages get a story showing the full assembly with representative props — not a story per 129 sub-section. 130 131 ### Categorisation 132 133 Story `title` drives the sidebar tree. Pick the first matching category: 134 135 | Category | What goes here | 136 | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 137 | `Foundation/` | Design tokens — Colour, Typography, Spacing, Icons, Shadows | 138 | `Elements/` | Generic building blocks — both display (Badge, Tag, Link, Avatar, Skeleton) and interactive controls (Button, Input, Checkbox, Select). Tiebreaker: _can it be used outside a form?_ → `Elements/`. | 139 | `Layout/` | Global chrome, navigation, and structural components — Header, Footer, DrawerMenu, ListMenu, Breadcrumb, Pagination, Seo | 140 | `Commerce/` | Commerce-specific shared components — ProductTile, OrderSummary, PromoCode, DisplayPrice, SwatchGroup | 141 | `Forms/` | Composed form assemblies — AddressForm, CheckoutContactForm, NewsletterSignup | 142 | `Pages/` | Full page assemblies — PDP, PLP, Cart, Checkout, Account | 143 | `Contentful/` | CMS-driven components — HeroBanner, RichText, ContentBlock. Use mock Contentful data in stories so variants are visible without a live CMS connection. | 144 145 Naming convention: singular for a concept or proper noun (`Foundation`, `Commerce`, `Layout`, `Contentful`); plural for a collection (`Elements`, `Forms`, `Pages`). 146 147 Examples: 148 149 ```ts 150 export default { title: 'Commerce/ProductTile' }; // ✅ 151 export default { title: 'Layout/Header' }; // ✅ 152 export default { title: 'Elements/Button' }; // ✅ 153 export default { title: 'Pages/PDP' }; // ✅ 154 export default { title: 'Elements/DisplayPrice' }; // ❌ — eCommerce specific, use Commerce/ 155 export default { title: 'Primitives/Button' }; // ❌ — use Elements/ 156 ``` 157 158 When in doubt: ask "what does this component _know_ about?" Commerce → `Commerce/`, 159 CMS-driven → `Contentful/`, nothing domain-specific → `Elements/`, page-level composition → `Pages/`. 160 161 ### Story content 162 163 - Every story file has a `Default` named export. 164 - Add named exports for meaningful states (`Loading`, `OutOfStock`, `WithDiscount`) — not 165 for every possible prop combination. 166 - `play` functions only when there's interactive behaviour worth asserting; otherwise the 167 story is purely visual. 168

Split out of [conventions.md](./conventions.md) — see that file for cross-cutting rules that apply to every file regardless of type (TypeScript-only, DRY/KISS/SOLID, magic numbers, security). TypeScript idioms live in [typescript.md](./typescript.md); Chakra/CSS conventions live in [css.md](./css.md). --- ## Components - **Named export** matches the folder name (e.g. `productTile/` exports `ProductTile`). No default exports of anonymous functions. - **Props type name** matches the component name: `ProductTileProps` for `ProductTile`, `TopNavProps` for `TopNav`. - **Props type placement:** - _Default:_ declare the `Props` type at the top of the component file. - _Move to `types.ts` in the same folder_ only when (a) the type is consumed by sibling files (story, test, sub-components) **or** (b) it exceeds ~30 lines and mixes with other shared types worth co-locating. - The trigger is _shared consumption_, not line count alone. - **JSDoc** is required on: - Any component used by ≥2 callers (shared components — typically Tier 2 in [protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md)). - Any exported hook. - Any utility function with non-obvious behaviour. Leaf components used by a single page don't need JSDoc — the prop type is sufficient. - **Callback props** follow `onEventName` (e.g. `onAddToCart`, `onClose`). - **Required props are non-optional;** optional props use `?` — no `| undefined` unions for "I forgot to mark it optional." - **Accessibility (JSX) — mechanically enforced by `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`, so get these right at authoring time:** - Every `` needs an `alt` attribute (`alt=""` is fine for purely decorative images). - Every `IconButton` (including wrapped variants like `IconButtonWithRegistration`) needs an `aria-label` — it renders no visible text, so screen readers have nothing else to announce. - Any element with an `onClick` that isn't natively interactive (`div`, `span`, `Box`, `Flex`, `Stack`, `VStack`, `HStack`, `Grid`, `Text`, and similar) needs a `role` attribute at minimum — and for real keyboard operability, also `tabIndex={0}` and an `onKeyDown` handler (or just use a `Button`/native interactive element instead, which is almost always simpler than reimplementing keyboard behaviour). --- ## Composition — writing a "clean" component Rules of thumb for when a component is doing too much and should be split, or when inline state belongs in a custom hook instead. - **Complexity / size.** A component function should stay roughly under ~150 lines and avoid deep branching (rule of thumb: ~10-15 cyclomatic complexity — count independent paths through the render logic, not total lines). **This is not currently ESLint-enforced** — `.eslintrc.js` has no `max-lines-per-function` or `complexity` rule configured today, so treat this as a self-check during authoring and something `/code-quality` should flag, not something the build will fail on yet. If this keeps being a problem in practice, adding those two ESLint rules is a cheap follow-up (they're built into ESLint core, no new dependency needed). - **Container/presentational separation.** Anything under `overrides/app/components/` receives data as props — it does not call data-fetching hooks itself (SDK hooks like `useCurrentBasket`/`useCurrentCustomer`/`useProduct`, or any `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` / React Query hook). Data-fetching belongs in `overrides/app/pages/` or another container component, which then passes the result down. This generalizes the existing "no commerce state hooks inside leaf components" rule to _all_ data-fetching, not just commerce SDK hooks — the reasoning is the same either way: a component that owns its own data-fetching can't be reused somewhere the data arrives differently (SSR-prefetched, mocked in Storybook, composed from a parent that already has it). **Exception — Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks** (`useIntl`, `useUiCopy`) may be called from any component, including presentational leaves. Both read from a Provider mounted above the route tree, not from a per-page/per-component fetch — so calling one from a leaf doesn't create the SSR/Storybook/parent-composition problem the rule above exists to prevent, and doesn't multiply fetches the way an SDK hook would. `useUiCopy` (`overrides/app/hooks/useUiCopy.ts`, Provider at `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/`) is the reference example — `BottomBar` and `ZimmSubscribeSection` both call it directly for microcopy while still receiving their actual business data as props. This exception is narrow: it covers content that is identical for every consumer regardless of route/context, not anything that varies per page. **Their no-Provider behaviour differs, and it matters for tests and stories.** `useUiCopy` degrades to fallback text — `useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY` — so a leaf calling it renders with zero setup. `useIntl` **throws** (`react-intl`'s `invariantIntlContext`: _"Could not find required `intl` object"_), and its `IntlProvider` is mounted by the **base SFCC `_app`**, not by `_app-config` — a strictly narrower subtree. `.storybook/preview.tsx` supplies one for stories precisely because of this; any Vitest test rendering a `useIntl` consumer must wrap it too. An earlier revision of this paragraph claimed both hooks degrade gracefully and that both Providers sit in `_app-config`; neither is true of `useIntl`. - **Extract-to-hook threshold.** Pull inline component logic out into a custom hook (`overrides/app/hooks/use.ts`) when either is true: - The component has ≥2 pieces of related `useState` that change together (a strong signal the state belongs in one place, whether that's a custom hook or a single reducer). - Any `useEffect` has a non-trivial dependency array or a cleanup function — non-trivial meaning more than a single obvious dependency, or the effect does anything beyond a one-line side effect. This one is judgment-heavy, not a hard mechanical gate — `/code-quality` should flag it as a should-fix, not a must-fix, and a component with ≥4 `useState` calls is a reasonable coarse trigger to at least stop and ask "should this be a hook?" --- ## Hooks - **File extension** is `.ts` (no JSX in a hook file). - **Exported function name** matches the filename: `useWishlist.ts` exports `useWishlist`. - **Parameters and return value are typed** — no implicit `any`, no missing return type. See [typescript.md](./typescript.md) for the general typing rules this extends. - **JSDoc** is required on every exported hook, including a `@returns` description. --- ## Storybook Storybook is the canonical place to view components in isolation. Keep it browsable — a flat 200-story sidebar is unusable. ### When a story is required - **Required** for any component exported from its folder under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/` (i.e. anything another file imports). - **Not required** for purely internal sub-components that only render inside one parent (e.g. `productTile/priceRow.tsx` used only by `productTile/index.tsx`). Cover their variants via the parent's stories. - Pages get a story showing the full assembly with representative props — not a story per sub-section. ### Categorisation Story `title` drives the sidebar tree. Pick the first matching category: | Category | What goes here | | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `Foundation/` | Design tokens — Colour, Typography, Spacing, Icons, Shadows | | `Elements/` | Generic building blocks — both display (Badge, Tag, Link, Avatar, Skeleton) and interactive controls (Button, Input, Checkbox, Select). Tiebreaker: _can it be used outside a form?_ → `Elements/`. | | `Layout/` | Global chrome, navigation, and structural components — Header, Footer, DrawerMenu, ListMenu, Breadcrumb, Pagination, Seo | | `Commerce/` | Commerce-specific shared components — ProductTile, OrderSummary, PromoCode, DisplayPrice, SwatchGroup | | `Forms/` | Composed form assemblies — AddressForm, CheckoutContactForm, NewsletterSignup | | `Pages/` | Full page assemblies — PDP, PLP, Cart, Checkout, Account | | `Contentful/` | CMS-driven components — HeroBanner, RichText, ContentBlock. Use mock Contentful data in stories so variants are visible without a live CMS connection. | Naming convention: singular for a concept or proper noun (`Foundation`, `Commerce`, `Layout`, `Contentful`); plural for a collection (`Elements`, `Forms`, `Pages`). Examples: ```ts export default { title: 'Commerce/ProductTile' }; // ✅ export default { title: 'Layout/Header' }; // ✅ export default { title: 'Elements/Button' }; // ✅ export default { title: 'Pages/PDP' }; // ✅ export default { title: 'Elements/DisplayPrice' }; // ❌ — eCommerce specific, use Commerce/ export default { title: 'Primitives/Button' }; // ❌ — use Elements/ ``` When in doubt: ask "what does this component _know_ about?" Commerce → `Commerce/`, CMS-driven → `Contentful/`, nothing domain-specific → `Elements/`, page-level composition → `Pages/`. ### Story content - Every story file has a `Default` named export. - Add named exports for meaningful states (`Loading`, `OutOfStock`, `WithDiscount`) — not for every possible prop combination. - `play` functions only when there's interactive behaviour worth asserting; otherwise the story is purely visual.

225	  (ZimmProductCardPlpVariation | ZimmProductCardHomeVariation | ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation);

228	  | ZimmProductCardPlpVariation['variation']
229	  | ZimmProductCardHomeVariation['variation']
230	  | ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation['variation'];

234	 * branch is actually active, purely so the component body below can destructure once with no
235	 * `if`/`switch` on `props.variation` — the extensibility AC requires every layout/visibility
236	 * decision to come from `VARIATION_CONFIG`, keyed by the discriminant, never a branching
237	 * statement. The exported `ZimmProductCardProps` discriminated union above is what actually
238	 * enforces correct usage at every call site (proven by the `@ts-expect-error` cases in
239	 * index.test.tsx) — this cast only relaxes internal access inside this file; it changes nothing
240	 * about what a caller may legally pass in.
241	 */

243	  Omit<ZimmProductCardPlpVariation, 'variation'> &
244	    Omit<ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation, 'variation'> &
245	    Omit<ZimmProductCardHomeVariation, 'variation'>
246	>;

248	type ZimmProductCardVariationConfig = {
249	  showBag: boolean;
250	  showAttributes: boolean;
251	  showSizeChips: boolean;
252	  /** PLP/Wishlist: price is visible by default and hides on hover. */
253	  hoverHidesPrice: boolean;
254	  /** Home only: price is hidden by default and reveals on hover. */
255	  hoverRevealsPrice: boolean;
256	  /** PLP/Wishlist: the size-chip picker is hidden by default and reveals on hover. */
257	  hoverRevealsSizeSelector: boolean;
258	  showRemove: boolean;
259	  /** PLP only (found during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit): Figma's Mobile Card-content
260	   *  instance has the bag icon's `Icons` frame `hidden="true"`, unlike Desktop and unlike
261	   *  Wishlist's own Mobile instance (bag stays visible there on every breakpoint). A viewport-
262	   *  width concern, not a hover one — see zimmProductCard.css.ts's own responsive rule. */
263	  hideBagOnMobile: boolean;
264	  /** Wishlist only (found during the follow-up full-sweep visual audit against every variant x
265	   *  state node): unlike PLP's unconditional `hideBagOnMobile`, Wishlist's Mobile Card-content
266	   *  instance shows the bag icon when available (`40002187:58470`) and hides it
267	   *  (`Icons` frame `hidden="true"`) only when unavailable (`40002187:58473`) — narrower than
268	   *  `hideBagOnMobile`, and combined with it (not replacing it) in the `bagHiddenOnMobile`
269	   *  derivation below, since the two are mutually exclusive per variation today but there is no
270	   *  reason to assume that stays true forever. */
271	  hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: boolean;
272	  /** Shown on PLP/Wishlist, suppressed on Home — see the module docblock's "Badge" note. */
273	  showBadge: boolean;
274	  /**

276	   * on Home per Dani Rivett's scope note, overriding the AC's unconditional framing — see the
277	   * module docblock's "Hover image-swap on Home" note. `false` here means a supplied
278	   * `hoverImage` is simply never swapped to, regardless of pointer capability.
279	   */
280	  showHoverImageSwap: boolean;

283	/**
284	 * The extensibility AC's actual mechanism: every layout/visibility decision this organism makes
285	 * reads from this table, keyed by `variation` — adding a future variation means adding a union
286	 * member above and one row here, touching no JSX. `index.tsx`'s render body contains no
287	 * `switch`/`if` on `props.variation` anywhere (verify with
288	 * `grep -n 'variation ===\|switch (variation)' index.tsx` — zero hits).
289	 */

291	  home: {
292	    showBag: false,
293	    showAttributes: false,
294	    showSizeChips: false,
295	    hoverHidesPrice: false,
296	    hoverRevealsPrice: true,
297	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: false,
298	    showRemove: false,
299	    hideBagOnMobile: false,
300	    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: false,
301	    showBadge: false,
302	    showHoverImageSwap: false,
303	  },
304	  plp: {
305	    showBag: true,
306	    showAttributes: false,
307	    showSizeChips: true,
308	    hoverHidesPrice: true,
309	    hoverRevealsPrice: false,
310	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: true,
311	    showRemove: false,
312	    hideBagOnMobile: true,
313	    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: false,
314	    showBadge: true,
315	    showHoverImageSwap: true,
316	  },
317	  wishlist: {
318	    showBag: true,
319	    showAttributes: true,
320	    showSizeChips: true,
321	    hoverHidesPrice: true,
322	    hoverRevealsPrice: false,
323	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: true,
324	    showRemove: true,
325	    hideBagOnMobile: false,
326	    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: true,
327	    showBadge: true,
328	    showHoverImageSwap: true,

332	const messages = defineMessages({
333	  // Interpolated with the product name, matching ZimmProductPrice's WAS/NOW pattern — Media's

346	 * across the `home` / `plp` / `wishlist` variations. See the module docblock above for the
347	 * confirmed Figma variation matrix and this component's own recipe (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) for
348	 * the stretched-link and hover-reveal mechanics that live entirely in CSS, not in this render
349	 * body — both children are always rendered in full, with every one of their own sub-parts; CSS
350	 * alone decides what is visible for a given variation and pointer capability.
351	 *
352	 * @param props see `ZimmProductCardProps` — a discriminated union on `variation`.
353	 */
354	export const ZimmProductCard = (props: ZimmProductCardProps) => {
355	  const {
356	    id,
357	    href,
358	    name,
359	    headingLevel,
360	    primaryImage,
361	    hoverImage,
362	    images,
363	    currentPrice,
364	    originalPrice,
365	    isPriceLoading,
366	    isUnavailable,
367	    onNotifyMe,
368	    badge,
369	    variation,
370	  } = props;
371	
372	  const { onAddToBag, sizeChipValues, selectedSizeChipValue, onSizeChipSelect, colour, size, onRemove } =
373	    props as ZimmProductCardVariationFields;
374	
375	  const intl = useIntl();
376	  const config = VARIATION_CONFIG[variation];
377	
378	  // Both conditions required — an organism that sets isUnavailable without a real callback
379	  // should not show a dead notify-me button. Mirrors ZimmProductCardContent's own
380	  // showNotifyMeButton co-requirement.
381	  const showNotifyMe = Boolean(isUnavailable) && Boolean(onNotifyMe);
382	
383	  // Fix C (SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit): confirmed against the real Figma Default+Hover
384	  // instances for every variation × Unavailable=True (including the Mobile/no-hover variants,
385	  // which show the only state a touch pointer ever sees) that `isUnavailable` suppresses the
386	  // size-selector hover-swap entirely — there is nothing to pick for an out-of-stock item, so
387	  // price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced. Home's own hover-reveals-price
388	  // behaviour is untouched by this — Home's Unavailable Hover reference (node 40002163:39990)
389	  // still reveals price on hover exactly as the in-stock case does; only the PLP/Wishlist
390	  // hide-and-swap needs suppressing.
391	  //
392	  // Suppressing `hoverRevealsSizeSelector` alone is not enough to reproduce that reference: it
393	  // only stops the organism adding its OWN hide/reveal pair, which leaves the size-chip wrapper
394	  // at Content's own natural (visible) default — briefly shipped that way mid-fix and caught by
395	  // re-checking the real Storybook render against Figma, which confirms size chips stay hidden
396	  // in BOTH states when unavailable, not just "not swapped in on hover". `sizeSelectorUnavailable`
397	  // carries that permanent hide separately, unconditional (not gated by hover-capability at all —
398	  // this isn't a pointer-type concern, unlike everything else in this recipe).
399	  //
400	  // Follow-up (full-sweep visual audit against every variant x state node, not just the sampled
401	  // set the first pass checked): `sizeSelectorUnavailable` ALSO drives a mobile-only price hide
402	  // in the recipe now (Fix F) — confirmed via `get_metadata` that Mobile PLP/Wishlist Unavailable
403	  // hide price and show notify-me in its place (`40002163:41488`, `40002187:58475`), the OPPOSITE
404	  // of Desktop's additive treatment (price stays, notify-me is simply added on hover). Nothing
405	  // extra is computed here for it — the recipe reads the same `sizeSelectorUnavailable` boolean
406	  // for both the size-chip permanent-hide and this new price rule, since both only ever apply to
407	  // the same PLP/Wishlist-and-unavailable case.
408	  const hoverHidesPrice = config.hoverHidesPrice && !isUnavailable;
409	  const hoverRevealsSizeSelector = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && !isUnavailable;
410	  const sizeSelectorUnavailable = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && Boolean(isUnavailable);
411	
412	  // Fix G (same follow-up audit): Wishlist-only. `hideBagOnMobile` alone only covers PLP's own
413	  // unconditional mobile hide; Wishlist's bag stays visible on mobile UNLESS unavailable
414	  // (`40002187:58470` vs `40002187:58473`). Combined into one boolean here rather than exposing
415	  // both conditions to the recipe — it only needs to know "hide this on mobile for this render",
416	  // not why.
417	  const bagHiddenOnMobile = config.hideBagOnMobile || (config.hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable && Boolean(isUnavailable));
418	
419	  const removeLabel = config.showRemove ? intl.formatMessage(messages.removeFromWishlist, { name }) : undefined;
420	  const resolvedBadge = config.showBadge ? badge : undefined;
421	
422	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_RECIPE, {
423	    hoverHidesPrice,
424	    hoverRevealsPrice: config.hoverRevealsPrice,
425	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector,
426	    sizeSelectorUnavailable,
427	    // Same Fix C audit: notify-me is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default,
428	    // revealed on hover/focus-visible — every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference shows it
429	    // appearing only there) but unconditionally visible on touch (every Mobile Unavailable
430	    // reference — the only state a touch pointer ever sees, per the "Mobile has no Hover variant"
431	    // finding — shows it plainly, with no hover to reveal it). This flag is deliberately keyed off
432	    // `showNotifyMe` itself, not `variation`: the confirmed behaviour is identical across all
433	    // three variations, and the recipe's selector simply matches nothing when notify-me isn't
434	    // mounted at all.
435	    hoverRevealsNotifyMe: showNotifyMe,
436	    hideBagOnMobile: bagHiddenOnMobile,
437	  });

439	  return (

441	      <ZimmProductCardMedia
442	        primaryImage={primaryImage}
443	        hoverImage={hoverImage}
444	        images={images}
445	        swapOnHover={config.showHoverImageSwap && Boolean(hoverImage)}
446	        showControls
447	        badge={resolvedBadge}
448	        onRemove={onRemove}
449	        removeLabel={removeLabel}
450	      />
451	      <ZimmProductCardContent
452	        name={name}
453	        headingLevel={headingLevel}
454	        href={href}
455	        currentPrice={currentPrice}
456	        originalPrice={originalPrice}
457	        isPriceLoading={isPriceLoading}
458	        showAttributes={config.showAttributes}
459	        colour={colour}
460	        size={size}
461	        showBag={config.showBag}
462	        isUnavailable={isUnavailable}
463	        onAddToBag={onAddToBag}
464	        showSizeChips={config.showSizeChips}
465	        sizeChipValues={sizeChipValues}
466	        selectedSizeChipValue={selectedSizeChipValue}
467	        onSizeChipSelect={onSizeChipSelect}
468	        showNotifyMe={showNotifyMe}
469	        onNotifyMe={onNotifyMe}
470	      />
471	    </chakra.div>
472	  );
473	};

import { breakpoints } from 'app/theme/foundation';

/**
 * Shared DOM-contract constants for the ZimmProductCard organism and its composed molecules
 * (ZimmProductCardMedia, ZimmProductCardContent) — defined once here so every producer (the JSX
 * that stamps a `data-card-slot` attribute) and consumer (the organism's own recipe selectors,
 * plus this component family's test suites) reads the same value instead of each independently
 * retyping it. Same pattern, smaller scale, as `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts`.
 */

/**
 * The ten `data-card-slot` attribute values that wire the organism's hover/reveal CSS
 * (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) to specific descendant DOM nodes. `media` / `badge` / `close` /
 * `carousel` / `indicator` are stamped by `ZimmProductCardMedia`; `content` / `bag` / `price` /
 * `sizeChips` / `notifyMe` by `ZimmProductCardContent`. Do not rename a value here without
 * checking both molecules' own docblocks, which document what each slot is for.
 */
export const CARD_SLOT = {
  media: 'media',
  badge: 'badge',
  close: 'close',
  carousel: 'carousel',
  indicator: 'indicator',
  content: 'content',
  bag: 'bag',
  price: 'price',
  sizeChips: 'sizeChips',
  notifyMe: 'notifyMe',
} as const;

/**
 * Hover-capable-pointer gate shared by every hover-only affordance across the card family
 * (desktop arrows, the hover-reveal price/size-selector swap, the notify-me reveal) — the
 * resolved SFCC-236 decision that arrows and the touch slide-indicator are mutually exclusive by
 * pointer capability, not viewport width.
 */
export const HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY = '@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)';

/**
 * Desktop viewport-width gate shared by the two places with a real min-width-driven layout
 * change: the organism's own PLP bag-icon mobile hide (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) and
 * `ZimmProductCardContent`'s responsive outer padding (`zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`).
 * Extracted for the identical reason `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above was — each file previously
 * derived this independently from the same `breakpoints.md` token, which is exactly the
 * same-value-typed-twice drift risk a shared constant removes.
 */
export const DESKTOP_QUERY = `@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`;

# Findings

## 1. `overrides/app/pages/home/` — exists, and is NOT blank in source

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx` exists (204 lines, last modified 2026‑09‑04, no sibling `index.stories.tsx` or `index.test.tsx` — worth noting since `.claude/rules/components.md` requires a story for anything exported from a folder under `overrides/app/pages/`). It is a real, working container, not a stub. Full render tree:

- `Home` → renders `Seo` + branches on a `?entry=` query param: if present, `HomePreviewContent` (Contentful Live Preview draft mode via `useContentfulEntry`); otherwise `HomeNormal`.
- `HomeNormal` → calls `useEinstein().sendViewPage`, sets SSR `Cache-Control`, then `useContentfulEntries<HomepageEntry>('homepage')`. While loading: a centered `Spinner`. **If no Contentful `homepage` entry resolves, it returns `null`** — this is almost certainly what "blank homepage" refers to: the *source* isn't empty, but the *rendered page* is genuinely blank (nothing but invisible `Seo` tags) whenever the CMS has no published `homepage` entry for the current site/locale.
- `HomepageContent` (shared by both normal and preview paths) → calls `useProductSearch` (see Q3 detail below) and renders a `Section` + `ProductScroller` with `productSearchResult?.hits`, but **only when `productSearchResult` is truthy** — no loading skeleton for this part, so it's blank during the fetch too.

Diff vs. base (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/home/index.jsx`, 336 lines): the override **removes** the base's static `Hero`, the `heroFeatures` grid, the `features` grid, and the "We're here to help" section (all sourced from local `./data.js`, which the override doesn't import at all), and **removes** the base's `Island hydrateOn={'visible'}` hydration wrappers and its `useDataCloud().sendViewPage` call. It **replaces** all of that with the Contentful entry-gating described above, keeping only the "Shop Products" `useProductSearch` section, which is otherwise nearly identical to base (same category/limit constants, same `expand` list plus `custom_properties`). Both versions keep `data-testid="home-page"` and `Home.getTemplateName = () => 'home'`; the override drops the base's screen-reader-only `<Heading as="h1">`.

## 2. `overrides/app/routes.tsx` — already registers `/` → the override home; no edit needed for an in-page demo

Full contents read (72 lines, Tier 2 — see Q6). The route list, in order:

```
'/'                    → Home            (loadable ./pages/home)
'/my-new-route'        → MyNewRoute
'/product/:productId'  → ProductDetail   (loadable ./pages/product-detail — explicit override entry, since the overrides resolver only redirects `@salesforce/retail-react-app`-named imports, not base's own relative `./pages/product-detail`)
..._routes                                (spreads in the ENTIRE base retail-react-app route array, imported as `routes as _routes` from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/routes`)
'/preview'             → ContentfulPreview
'/:slug'               → Experience       (Contentful Studio catch-all fallback)
```

`configureRoutes(routes, config, { ignoredRoutes: ['/callback', '*'] })` merges/dedupes this against the base array, keeping the **first** match — which is why `/` and `/product/:productId` are declared before `..._routes` (base also declares a `/` and a `/product/:productId`).

**Answer: the homepage route already resolves through this repo's own `routes.tsx`, pointing at `overrides/app/pages/home`.** Since your plan is to extend the *existing* home page with a demo section, you do not need to touch `routes.tsx` at all — it's already correctly wired. You would only need to touch it if you instead wanted a **separate, distinct** route (e.g. `/product-card-demo`) rather than embedding the demo in `/`.

## 3. Best existing container pattern — `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`

Read in full (1168 lines). Confirmed hooks, all from `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`:

```ts
import {
  useProduct, useProducts, useCategory,
  useShopperCustomersMutation,
  useShopperBasketsV2Mutation as useShopperBasketsMutation,
  useCustomerId,
  useShopperBasketsV2MutationHelper as useShopperBasketsMutationHelper,
} from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
```

- `useProduct` — single product by ID (detailed in Q4).
- `useProducts` (plural) — fetches child variant products for sets/bundles by comma-joined `ids`.
- `useCategory` — fetches the primary category, gated on `productResponse?.primaryCategoryId` (dependent query).
- The mutation/customer hooks are for basket/wishlist writes, not relevant to a read-only demo.

**Data shape**: the codebase does **not** type these responses — `type SfccProduct = any` (and `SfccVariant`, `SfccCategory` likewise), with an explicit in-file comment acknowledging `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` does export `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`/`.Variant`/`.Category` and that using them is a deferred gap, not proof no type exists. Real fields accessed throughout: `id`, `name`, `longDescription`, `master.masterId`, `currency`, `primaryCategoryId`, `type.{set,bundle,master,item}`, `variants[]` (`productId`, `variationValues`, `tieredPrices`), `childProducts[]`, `setProducts`, `pageTitle`, `pageDescription`, `pageMetaTags[]`, `price`, `imageGroups` (confirmed passed at `product-view/index.tsx:731`), plus Zimmermann `c_*` custom attributes (`c_modelFit`, `c_careInstructions`, `c_color`, `c_colourId`, `c_environmentalNotes`, `c_fabricComposition`, `c_hsCode`, `c_sizeFit`, `c_styleId`, `c_styleNumber`, `c_stylingNotes`, `c_tabDescription.markup`, `c_tabDetails.markup`, `c_relatedSwatches[]`).

**Dedicated mapper file**: yes — `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts`, exporting:
- `selectPdpProductInfo(product, priceData, currency, formatPrice): PdpProductInfo | null` — pure function (no React/react-intl import), takes `formatPrice` as an **injected function parameter** so the module itself stays framework-free and independently unit-testable (`productInfo.test.ts`). Maps the raw `c_*`/name/description fields onto a flat `PdpProductInfo` shape (`name`, `price`, `wasPrice`, `description`, `modelInfo`, `careInstructions`, `styleCode`, `colour`, `colourId`, etc.).
- `buildRelatedSwatches(rawSwatches, urlBuilder, colourAttrId)` — maps `c_relatedSwatches[]` onto swatch-group-compatible values.

Note: on the page itself, `selectPdpProductInfo`'s `formatPrice` branch is a documented dead path (`priceData` is passed `null`) — the **live** price path is a second, parallel pipeline: `variantScopedPrice.ts`'s `selectVariantScopedPriceData()` (calls base's `getPriceData` from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils`) → passed into `ProductView`'s `renderHeader` → into `partials/staticProductHeader.tsx`, which holds its own `useIntl()` and its own local `formatPrice` closure (detailed in Q5).

## 4. `useProduct` — real signature/return as used in this codebase

```ts
const {
  data: productResponse,
  isLoading: isProductLoading,
  isError: isProductError,
  error: productError,
} = useProduct(
  {
    parameters: {
      id: requestedProductId,                 // string — the only required param in practice
      perPricebook: true,
      expand: [
        'availability', 'promotions', 'options', 'images', 'prices',
        'variations', 'set_products', 'bundled_products', 'page_meta_tags',
      ],
      allImages: true,
      ...(selectedInventoryId ? { inventoryIds: selectedInventoryId } : {}),
    },
  },
  { keepPreviousData: true },   // React Query option — old data stays rendered during a variant refetch
);
```

Standard React Query shape: `{ data, isLoading, isError, error }`, `data` untyped (`any`) in this codebase as noted above. This is the hook you'd use for a single product by ID/slug for the demo page — same call shape, just swap `id` for whatever product ID(s) you pick to demonstrate.

**Image field for `ZimmProductCardProps`**: confirmed `product.imageGroups` is the real field (used at `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:731`, passed straight through — there is no override of SFCC's `ImageGallery`/image-extraction logic in this repo; `overrides/app/components/image-gallery/` does **not** exist on disk despite being named in `protectedFiles.md`, see Q6 note). Base retail-react-app's own `product-tile/index.jsx` shows the canonical extraction pattern you'd replicate for the demo mapper:

```js
import { filterImageGroups, getPriceData } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils'
import { useCurrency } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks'
...
const filteredImageGroups = filterImageGroups(imageGroups, {...})
// then per image: image?.disBaseLink || image.link   →  src
//                 image.alt                            →  alt
```

**No existing mapper from raw SFCC product → `ZimmProductCardProps` exists anywhere in this repo.** I checked `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/zimmProductCardShared.ts` (it looked promising by name) — it only holds `data-card-slot` DOM-attribute constants and shared media-query strings for the card family's own CSS/tests, not a data mapper. You'd be building this fresh, following `productInfo.ts`'s pattern (pure function, `formatPrice`/`urlBuilder` injected as params, unit-tested standalone).

## 5. Price formatting — no shared `formatPrice` utility in `utils/`; it's react-intl's `formatNumber`, called locally at each render site

`overrides/app/utils/` contains: `richText.tsx`, `contentfulImage.ts`, `resolveImageEntry.ts`, `safeHref.ts`, `resolveByRegion.ts`, `sfccImage.ts` — **no** price/currency file.

The actual pipeline, confirmed at the one **live** call site (`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/staticProductHeader.tsx`):

```ts
const { formatNumber } = useIntl();
const formatPrice = (amount: number, priceCurrency: string) =>
  formatNumber(amount, { style: 'currency', currency: priceCurrency });
```

i.e. it's react-intl's built-in `formatNumber({style: 'currency', ...})`, wrapped in a locally-declared closure, redeclared independently in both `staticProductHeader.tsx` (live) and `product-detail/index.tsx` (present but dead — its `priceData` arg is always `null`, per an explicit code comment). This is **not** DRY today — the same one-line wrapper exists in two places with a comment explaining why they can't drift (only one ever executes) rather than a shared export.

The raw numbers themselves come from base's `getPriceData()` (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils`), which `variantScopedPrice.ts` calls and which returns `{ currentPrice, listPrice, isOnSale, isRange }` — `formatPrice` is applied to `.currentPrice`/`.listPrice` afterward to produce the final strings.

`use-currency.ts` — named in `protectedFiles.md`'s Tier 2 "Shared Hooks" list (`overrides/app/hooks/use-currency.ts`) — **does not exist on disk**. The actual `useCurrency` in use (`product-view/index.tsx:53,310`) is imported straight from base: `import { useCurrency } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks'`, and only returns `{ currency: activeCurrency }` (an ISO code like `'USD'`), not a formatted string — it feeds the `currency` arg to `formatNumber`, it doesn't format anything itself.

Confirmed at the `ZimmProductCard` type/story level that this whole chain expects **pre-formatted strings**, exactly as you described: `ZimmProductCardBaseProps.currentPrice?: string` / `originalPrice?: string`, and `index.stories.tsx` passes literals like `currentPrice: '$595.00'`, `originalPrice: '$595.00'` / `currentPrice: '$416.50'` for the sale-price story.
